To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the results exclude WIMP-nucleon cross section above 3.0×10-43 cm2 for a WIMP with a mass of 60 GeV, and that the exclusion limit starts to reach the CMSSM region.
we have excluded a spin‐aver‐aged WIMP‐Ge interaction cross section above the 90%C.L of 1.6×10−43 cm for a WIMP of mass 60 Ge V/c2.
we have excluded the parameter space of minimal super symmetric models (MSSMs) and constrained models (CMSSMs) for WIMP masses 60 GeV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of dark matter, which is a key problem in modern physics.
the development of new techniques to improve the sensitivity of the experiment to WIMP detection.
the search for the dark matter in the universe.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Cryogenic Dark matter search has excluded the possibility that the WIMP is a Ge or Si isotope with a cross section larger than the values given above.
the CDMS experiment is not able to detect WIMP‐nuclear scattering with the present experimental setup.
we are still searching for dark matter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MSSM parameter space is now constrained by our results.
the MSSM parameter space is excluded by the CDMS experiment, but the CMSSM is not excluded.
the CDMS Soudan experiment excludes a spin‐averaved WIMP‐nuclear cross section greater than 2.5 × 10−42 cm2 at 90%C.L for a WIMP with a mass of 60 GeV/2c2.

we have demonstrated the feasibility of using Ge detectors for dark matter search.
